# dgttrs

> Solves one of the systems of equations A·X = B or Aᵀ·X = B, with a tridiagonal matrix A using the LU factorization computed by DGTTRF.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dgttrs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dgttrs';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dgttrs(
    order,
    trans,
    N, nrhs,
    DL, strideDL,
    d, strideD,
    DU, strideDU,
    DU2, strideDU2,
    IPIV, strideIPIV,
    B, LDB
) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | Specifies the form of the system of equations. `'no-transpose'`: A \* X = B (No transpose) `'transpose'`: A\*\*T\* X = B (Transpose)<br>One of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'`. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The order of the matrix A.<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B.<br>Requires `nrhs ≥ 0` |
| `DL` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | The (n-1) multipliers that define the matrix L from the LU factorization of A. |
| ↳ `strideDL` | `integer` | Stride length for `DL` |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | The n diagonal elements of the upper triangular matrix U from the LU factorization of A. |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| `DU` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | The (n-1) elements of the first super-diagonal of U. |
| ↳ `strideDU` | `integer` | Stride length for `DU` |
| `DU2` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 2</sub> | The (n-2) elements of the second super-diagonal of U. |
| ↳ `strideDU2` | `integer` | Stride length for `DU2` |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | The pivot indices; for 1 <= i <= n, row i of the matrix was interchanged with row IPIV(i) (0-based). |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | Stride length for `IPIV` |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>max(N, 1) × nrhs</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, the matrix of right hand side vectors B. On exit, B is overwritten by the solution vectors X. |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `B`<br>Column-major requires `LDB ≥ max(N, 1)`<br>Row-major requires `LDB ≥ max(1, nrhs)` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations.

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$  (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Conjugate transpose = Transpose)
- `N`: The order of the matrix A.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `DL`: The (n-1) multipliers that define the matrix L from the LU factorization of A.
- `d`: The n diagonal elements of the upper triangular matrix U from the LU factorization of A.
- `DU`: The (n-1) elements of the first super-diagonal of U.
- `DU2`: The (n-2) elements of the second super-diagonal of U.
- `IPIV`: The pivot indices; for $1 \le i \le n$, row i of the matrix was interchanged with row `IPIV(i)`. `IPIV(i)` will always be either i or i+1; `IPIV(i) = i` indicates a row interchange was not required.
- `B`: On entry, the matrix of right hand side vectors B. On exit, B is overwritten by the solution vectors X.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( N, 1 )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` sixteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dgttrs.ndarray(
    trans,
    N, nrhs,
    DL, strideDL, offsetDL,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    DU, strideDU, offsetDU,
    DU2, strideDU2, offsetDU2,
    IPIV, strideIPIV, offsetIPIV,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB
) → info: integer
```

Solves one of the systems of equations A_X = B or A^T_X = B with a.
tridiagonal matrix A using the LU factorization computed by dgttrf.

## Notes

-   IPIV values are 0-based (Fortran convention is 1-based).
-   `trans` is a single character: `'no-transpose'` or `'transpose'`.
-   INFO is returned: 0 = success.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | `'no-transpose'` for A\*X=B, `'transpose'` for A^T\*X=B<br>One of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'`. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix A<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of right hand sides (columns of B)<br>Requires `nrhs ≥ 0` |
| `DL` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | Multipliers from LU factorization (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDL` | `integer` | Stride length for `DL` |
| ↳ `offsetDL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `DL` |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Diagonal of U (length N) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `d` |
| `DU` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | First superdiagonal of U (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDU` | `integer` | Stride length for `DU` |
| ↳ `offsetDU` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `DU` |
| `DU2` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 2</sub> | Second superdiagonal of U (length N-2) |
| ↳ `strideDU2` | `integer` | Stride length for `DU2` |
| ↳ `offsetDU2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `DU2` |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Pivot indices (length N), 0-based |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | Stride length for `IPIV` |
| ↳ `offsetIPIV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `IPIV` |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>max(N, 1) × nrhs</sub> | **in/out** · Right hand side matrix, overwritten with solution |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `B` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations.

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$  (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Conjugate transpose = Transpose)
- `N`: The order of the matrix A.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `DL`: The (n-1) multipliers that define the matrix L from the LU factorization of A.
- `d`: The n diagonal elements of the upper triangular matrix U from the LU factorization of A.
- `DU`: The (n-1) elements of the first super-diagonal of U.
- `DU2`: The (n-2) elements of the second super-diagonal of U.
- `IPIV`: The pivot indices; for $1 \le i \le n$, row i of the matrix was interchanged with row `IPIV(i)`. `IPIV(i)` will always be either i or i+1; `IPIV(i) = i` indicates a row interchange was not required.
- `B`: On entry, the matrix of right hand side vectors B. On exit, B is overwritten by the solution vectors X.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0 || nrhs === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dgttrf from './../../dgttrf/lib/index.js';
import dgttrs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dgttrs';

// Tridiagonal matrix A (N = 4); the right-hand side is b = A*[1,2,3,4]:
const N = 4;
const nrhs = 1;
const DL = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 ] );
const d = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 4.0, 4.0, 4.0 ] );
const DU = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 ] );
const DU2 = new Float64Array( N - 2 );
const IPIV = new Int32Array( N );

// Compute the LU factorization of A:
dgttrf( N, DL, 1, d, 1, DU, 1, DU2, 1, IPIV, 1 );

// Using the standard interface:
let B = new Float64Array( [ 6.0, 12.0, 18.0, 19.0 ] );
dgttrs( 'column-major', 'no-transpose', N, nrhs, DL, 1, d, 1, DU, 1, DU2, 1, IPIV, 1, B, N );
console.log( 'X:', B );

// Using the ndarray interface:
B = new Float64Array( [ 6.0, 12.0, 18.0, 19.0 ] );
dgttrs.ndarray( 'no-transpose', N, nrhs, DL, 1, 0, d, 1, 0, DU, 1, 0, DU2, 1, 0, IPIV, 1, 0, B, 1, N, 0 );
console.log( 'X:', B );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DGTTRS`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DGTTRS solves one of the systems of equations

$$
A \, X = B \quad\text{or}\quad A^T \, X = B
$$

with a tridiagonal matrix A using the LU factorization computed by DGTTRF.

</section>
